devverse:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामका: पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥ १ ॥
commentary: What did Pându's sons and mine do when they assembled together on the sacred plain of Kurukshetra, eager for battle, O Samjaya?
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 1

devverse:
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा ।
आचार्यमुपसंगम्य राजा वचनमत्रवीत् ॥ २ ॥
commentary: Having seen the army of the Påndavas drawn up in battle-array, prince Duryodhana then approached his teacher and spoke (these) words:
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 2

devverse:
पइयैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्यं महतीं चमूम् ।
ब्यदां द्रुपद्पुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥ ३ ॥
commentary: "O teacher, look at this grand army of the sons of Pându, marshalled by thy talented pupil, the son of Drupada.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 3

devverse:
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि ।
युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथ: ॥ ४ ॥
commentary: "Here are heroes, mighty archers, equal in battle to Bhîma and Arjuna,-Yuyudhâna, Virâta, and Drupada, the master of a great car (mahāratha).*
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 4

devverse:
घृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान ।
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥ ५ ॥
commentary: “Dhrishtaketu, Chekitâna, and the valiant king of Kâsi, Purujit and Kunti-Bhoja and that eminent man Saibya; "The heroic Yudhâmanyu and the brave Uttamaujas; the son of Subhadrâ and the sons of Draupadî, all masters of great cars (mahârathas).
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 5

devverse:
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् ।
सौमद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथा: ।। ६ ।।
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम ।
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्त्रवीमि ते ॥ ७ ॥
commentary: "But know, O best of the twice-born, who are the most distinguished among us, the leaders of my army; these I name to thee by way of example.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 7

devverse:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च क्रुपश्च समितिञ्चयः ।
अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमद्त्तिस्तथैव च ॥ ८ ॥
commentary: "Thyself and Bhîshma, and Karna, and also Kripa, the victor in war, Asvatthâman and Vikarna, and also Jayadratha, the son of Soma- datta ;
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 8

devverse:
अन्ये च बहव: शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।
नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥ ९ ॥
commentary: "And many other heroes who have given up their lives for my sake, fighting with various weapons, all well-skilled in battle.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 9

devverse:
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् ।
पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषाम् बळं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥ १० ॥
commentary: "This army of ours protected bv Bhîshma is inadequate, whereas that army of theirs which is under the protection of Bhîma is adequate.* "And therefore do ye all, occupying your respective positions in the several divisions of the army, support Bhîshma only."
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 10

devverse:
अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः ।
भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्वे एव हि ।। ११ ॥
तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः ।
सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चै: शङ्खं दथ्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥ १२ ॥
commentary: His mighty grandsire, (Bhîshma), the oldest of the Kauravas, in order to cheer him, sounded on high a lion's roar and blew his conch.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 12

devverse:
तत: राङ्काश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखा: ।
सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽमवत् ॥ १३ ॥
commentary: Then, all at once, conches and kettle- drums, cymbols, drums and horns were played upon, and the sound was a tumultuous uproar.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 13

devverse:
ततः श्वेतैईयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ ।
माधव: पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदृष्मतु: ॥ १४ ॥
commentary: Then, too, Màdhava and the son of Pându, seated in a grand chariot yoked to white horses, blew their celestial conches.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 14

devverse:
पाछ्रजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः ।
पौण्डूं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥ १५ ॥
commentary: Hrishîkesa blew the Pànchajanya, and Arjuna blew the Devadatta. Bhîma, (the doer) of terrible deeds, blew his great conch Paundra.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 15

devverse:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ।
नकुल: सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥ १६ ॥
commentary: Prince Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya, while Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and the Manipushpaka.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 16

devverse:
काइयश्च परमेष्वास: शिखण्डी च महारथ: ।
घृष्टचुम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥ १७ ॥
commentary: The king of Kâsî, an excellent archer, Sikhandin, the master of a great car, Dhrishta- dyumna and Virâta, and the unconquered Sâtyaki;
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 17

devverse:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः प्रथिवीपते ।
सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्कान्दन्मुः प्रथक्पृथक् ॥ १८ ॥
commentary: Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, O lord of earth, and the son of Subhadrà, of mighty arms, all together blew their respective conches.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 18

devverse:
स घोषो घार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् ।
नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुले व्यनुनादयन् ॥ १९ ॥
commentary: That tumultuous sound rent the hearts of (the people) of Dhritarâshtra's party, making both heaven and earth resound.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 19

devverse:
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिथ्वजः ।
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥ २० ॥
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 20

devverse:
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥ २१ ॥
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 21

devverse:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धकामानवस्थितान् ।
कैर्मया सह योद्घव्यमस्मित्रणसमुद्यमे ॥ २२ ॥
commentary: 20-22. Then seeing the people of Dhritarash- tra's party regularly marshalled, while the discharge of weapons began, Arjuna, the son of Påndu, whose ensign was a monkey, O King of earth, took up his bow and said thus to Krishna : “O Achyuta (Immortal), place my chariot between the two armies, that I may just see those who stand here desirous to fight, and know with whom I must fight in this strife of battle.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 22

devverse:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः ।
धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥ २३ ॥
commentary: "I will observe those who are assembled here and are about to engage in battle desirous to do service in war to the evil-minded son of Dhritarâshtra."
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 23

devverse:
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥ २४ ॥
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 24

devverse:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम ।
डवाच पार्थ पदयैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥ २५ ॥
commentary: 24-25. O descendant of Bharata, Hrishîkesa (Krishna) thus addressed by Gudâkesa (Arjuna) stationed that excellent car between the two armies in front of Bhishma and Drona and all the rulers of earth, and said : " O son of Prithà, look at these assembled Kauravas."
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 25

devverse:
तत्रापदयत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितृनथ पितामहान् ।
आचार्यान्मातुलान्ञ्रातृन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सर्खीस्तथा ॥ २६ ॥
commentary: 26-27. Then the son of Prithā saw arrayed there in both the armies fathers and grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and comrades, fathers-in-law and friends.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 26

devverse:
श्वद्युरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि ।
तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेय: सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥ २७ ॥
commentary: 27-28. When the son of Kunti saw all the kinsmen standing, he was overcome with deepest pity and said thus in sorrow :
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 27

devverse:
कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमत्रवीत् ।
दृष्ट्वेमं खजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥ २८ ॥
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 28

devverse:
सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिद्युष्यति ।
वेपधुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ २९ ॥
commentary: 28-29. Seeing these kinsmen, O Krishna, arrayed and desirous to fight, my limbs droop down, and my mouth is dried up. A tremor comes on my body and my hairs stand on end.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 29

devverse:
गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिद्द्यते ।
न च शक्तोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मन: ॥ ३० ॥
commentary: The Gāndīva slips from my hand, and my skin is intensely burning. I am also unable to stand and my mind is whirling round, as it were.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 30

devverse:
निमित्तानि च पत्र्यामि विपरीतानि केशव ।
न च श्रेयोऽनुपदयामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥ ३१ ॥
commentary: And, O Kesava, 1 see omens foreboding evil. Nor do I see any good from killing my kinsmen in battle. I desire not victory, O Krisna, nor king- dom, nor pleasures. Of what avail is dominion to us, O Govinda? Of what avail are pleasures and even life ?
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 31

devverse:
न काइक्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च ।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ।। ३२ ।।
येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च ।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्यक्तवा धनानि च ॥ ३.३ ॥
आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तयैव च पितामहाः ।
मातुलाः श्वश्लुराः पौत्राः स्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥ ३४ ॥
commentary: 33-34. They for whose sake dominion, enjoy- ments and pleasures are sought by us are here standing, having staked their life and wealth: teachers, fathers, sons as well as grandfathers; maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, bro- thers-in-law as also (other) relatives.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 34

devverse:
एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि न्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन ।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥ ३५ ॥
commentary: These, O slayer of Madhu, I do not wish to kill, though they kill me, even for the sake of dominion over the three worlds; how much less, for the sake of the earth!
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 35

devverse:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन ।
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥ ३६ ॥
commentary: O Janārdana, what delight shall be ours ર6 after killing the sons of Dhritasāshtra? On killing these felons, sin only will take hold of us.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 36

devverse:
तस्मान्नाही वयं हन्तुं घार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् ।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माघव ॥ ३७ ॥
commentary: We had then better not slay our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarāshtra; for, how can we be happy, O Màdhava, after slaying our own people ?
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 37

devverse:
यद्यप्येते न पत्रयन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः ।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥ ३८ ॥
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 38

devverse:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् ।
कुल्रक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपद्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥ ३९ ॥
commentary: 38-39. Though these, whose intelligence is stricken by greed, perceive no evil in the extinction of families and no sin in treachery to friends, yet, O Janārdana, should not we, who clearly see evil in the extinction of a family, learn to refrain from this sinful deed?
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 39

devverse:
क़ुलक्षये प्रणइयन्ति कुलघर्माः सनातनाः ।
घर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥ ४० ॥
commentary: On the extinction of a family, the imme- morial dharmas * of that family disappear. When the dharmas disappear, impiety (adharma) over- takes the whole family. +
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 40

devverse:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्रियः ।
स्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥ ४१ ॥
commentary: By the prevalence of impiety, O Krishna, the women of the family become corrupt. Women corrupted, there will be intermingling of castes (varna-samkara), O descendant of Vrishnis.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 41

devverse:
सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलन्नानां कुलस्य च ।
पतन्ति पितरो द्येषां छप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥ ४२ ॥
commentary: Confusion of castes leads the family of these destroyers of families also to hell; for, their forefathers fall (down to hell), deprived of the offerings of pinda (rice-ball) and water.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 42

devverse:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः ।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिघर्माः कळघर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥ ४३ ॥
commentary: By these evil deeds of the destroyers of families which cause the intermingling of castes, the eternal dharmas of castes and families are subverted.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 43

devverse:
उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन ।
नरके नियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुह्युश्रुम ॥ ४४ ॥
commentary: We have heard, O Janârdana, that neces- sary is the dwelling in hell of the men whose family dharmas are subverted.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 44

devverse:
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्।
यद्राज्यसुखळोभेन हन्तुं खजनमुद्यताः ॥ ४५ ॥
commentary: Alas! we have resolved to commit a great sin, inasmuch as we are endeavouring to slay our kinsmen out of a craving for the pleasures of dominion.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 45

devverse:
यदि मामप्रतीकारमञ्खं शखपाणय: ।
घार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥ ४६ ॥
commentary: It would be better for me, if the sons of Dhritarâshtra, with arms in hand, should slay me unarmed and unresisting in the battle.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 46

devverse:
एवमुक्तवाऽर्जुन: सङ्खये स्थोपस्थ उपाविशत् ।
विसृज्य सज्ञरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥ ४७ ॥
commentary: Having said thus, Arjuna, sorrow-stricken in mind, cast aside his bow and arrows in the midst of the battle and sat down in the chariot. SANKHYA YOGA.
ref: THE BHAGAVAD GITA -> THE DESPONDENCY OF ARJUNA -> 47

devverse:
तं तथा क्रुपयाऽऽविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् ।
विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥ १ ॥
commentary: To him who was thus overcome with pity and afflicted, and whose eyes were full of tears and agitated, the destroyer of Madhu spoke as follows:

devverse:
कुतस्त्वा कइमलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् ।
अनार्यज्रष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥ २ ॥
commentary: Whence in (this) perilous strait has come upon thee this weakness cherished by the unworthy, debarring from heaven and causing disgrace, O Arjuna?

devverse:
क्रैब्यं मा स्म गम: पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्य<del>त्त</del>्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥ ३ ॥
commentary: Yield not to unmanliness, O son of Prithâ. It does not become thee. Cast off this base weak- ness of heart and arise, O tormentor of foes

devverse:
कथं भीष्ममहं सङ्ख्ये द्रोणं च मघुसूदन ।
इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥ ४ ॥
commentary: O slayer of Madhu, how shall I assail in battle with arrows Bhishma and Drona, who are worthy of worship, O slayer of enemies.

devverse:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्
श्रेयो भोक्तुं मैंक्ष्यमपीह लोके ।
हत्वाऽर्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव
मुञ्जीय भोगात्रुघिरप्रदिग्घान् ॥ ५ ॥
commentary: Better indeed in this world to live even upon alms than to slay the teachers of high honor. But, were I to slay these teachers, I should only in this world enjoy the pleasures of wealth, delights stained with blood.

devverse:
न चैतदिद्याः कतरच्यो गरीयो
यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः ।
यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामः
तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे घार्तराष्ट्राः ॥ ६ ॥
commentary: And we know not which * is the better alternative for us; nor do we know whether we shall conquer them or they will conquer us. Even the sons of Dhritarâshtra, after killing whom we do not wish to live, stand arrayed against us.

devverse:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः
प्टच्छामि त्वां धर्मसम्मूढचेताः ।
यच्छ्रेय: स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे
शिल्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥ ७ ॥
commentary: My heart contaminated by the taint of helplessness, my mind confounded about Dharma,* I ask Thee: Tell me what is absolutely good. T am Thy pupil. Instruct me, who have sought Thy grace.

devverse:
न हि प्रपद्यामि ममापनुचादू-
यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् ।
अवाप्य भूमावसपन्नमृद्धं
राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥ ८ ॥
commentary: I do not indeed see what can dispel the grief which burns up my senses, even after attain- ing unrivalled and prosperous dominion on earth or even lordship over gods. Having spoken thus to Hrishikesa, Gudà- kesa, the tormenter of foes, said to Govinda, 'I will not fight,' and verily remained silent.

devverse:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्तवा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तपः ।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्तवा तूर्ष्णी बभूव ह ॥ ९ ||
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहुसन्निव भारत ।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मघ्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥ १० ॥
commentary: To him who was grieving in the midst of the two armies, O descendant of Bharata, Hrishi- kesa as if smiling, spoke these words :

devverse:
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे ।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥ ११ ॥
commentary: For those who deserve no grief thou hast grieved, and words of wisdom thou speakest. For the living and for the dead the wise grieve not.*

devverse:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥ १२ ॥
commentary: Never did I not exist, nor thou, nor these rulers of men; and no one of us will ever hereafter cease to exist.

devverse:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा ।
तया देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥ १३ ॥
commentary: Just as in this body the embodied (Self) passes into childhood and youth and old age, so does He pass into another body. There the wise man is not distressed.

devverse:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः ।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥ १४ ॥
commentary: The sense-contacts it is, O son of Kunti, which cause heat and cold; pleasure and pain; they come and go, they are impermanent. Them endure bravely, O descendant of Bharata.

devverse:
यं हि न व्यथयन्लेते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥ १५ ॥
commentary: That wise man whom, verily, these afflict not, O chief of men, to whom pleasure and pain are same, he for immortality is fit.

devverse:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ।
डभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तस्वदर्शिभिः ॥ १६ ॥
commentary: Of the unreal no being there is; there is no non being of the real. Of both these is fhe truth seen by the seers of the Essence.

devverse:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वेमिदं ततम् ।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥ १७ ॥
commentary: But know that to be imperishable by which all this is pervaded. None can cause the destruction of That, the Inexhaustible.

devverse:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः ।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥ १८ ॥
commentary: These bodies of the embodied (Self) who is eternal, indestructible and unknowable, are said to have an end. Do fight, therefore, O descendant of Bharata.

devverse:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं इन्ति न हन्यते ॥ १९ ॥
commentary: Whoever looks upon Him as the slayer, and whoever looks upon Him as the slain, both these know not aright. He slays not, nor is He slain

devverse:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचि-
न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥ २० ॥
commentary: He is not born, nor does He ever die; after having been, He again ceases not to be; nor the reverse. Unborn, eternal, unchangeable and primeval, He is not slain when the body is slain. Whoso knows Him as indestructible, eternal, unborn and inexhaustible,—How, O son of Prithâ, and whom does such a man cause to slay, and whom does he slay? Just as a man casts off worn-out clothes and puts on others which are new, so the embodied (Self) casts off worn-out bodies and enters others which are new.

devverse:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एतमजमव्ययम् ।
कथं स पुरुषः पार्थं कं घातयति हन्ति कम । २१ ॥
वासांसि जीणांनि यथा विद्दाय
नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि ।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा-
न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही || २२ ||
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावक: ।
न चैनं छेदयन्त्यापो न शाषयति मारुतः ॥ २३ ॥
commentary: Him weapons cut not, Him fire burns not, and Him water wets not; Him wind dries not.

devverse:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाद्योऽयमक्केद्योऽशोष्य एव च ।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥ २४ ॥
commentary: He cannot be cut, nor burnt, nor wetted, nor dried up. He is everlasting, all-pervading stable, firm, and eternal.

devverse:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमु<del>च्यतः</del>
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुज्ञोचितुमईसि ॥ २५ ॥
commentary: He, it is said, is unmanifest, unthinkable and unchangeable. Wherefore, knowing Him to be such, thou hadst better grieve not.

devverse:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् ।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैनं शोचितमईसि ॥ २६ ॥
commentary: But even if thou thinkest of Him as ever being born and ever dying, even then, O mighty-armed, thou oughtst not to grieve thus.

devverse:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्धुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ।
तस्माद्परिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमईसि ॥ २७ ॥
commentary: To that which is born, death is indeed certain; and to that which is dead, birth is certain. Wherefore, about the unavoidable thing, thou oughtst not to grieve.

devverse:
अव्यक्तादानि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत ।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥ २८ ॥
commentary: Beings have their beginning unseen, their middle seen, and their end unseen again. Why any lamentation regarding them ? One sees Him as a wonder; and so also another speaks of him as a wonder; and as a wonder another hears of Him; and though hearing, none understands Him at all.

devverse:
आश्चर्यवत्पदयति कश्चिदेन-
माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः ।
आश्चर्यवचैनमन्यः श्रणोति
श्रुत्वाऽप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चिन् ॥ २९ ।
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत ।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोवितुमर्हेसि ॥ ३० ॥
commentary: He, the embodied (Self) in every one's body, can never be killed, O descendant of Bharata. Wherefore thou oughtst not to grieve about any creature.

devverse:
खधर्ममापे चावेल्य न बिकम्पितुमईसि ।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥ ३१ ॥
commentary: Having regard to thine own duty also, thou oughtst not to waver. For, to a Kshatriya, there is nothing more wholesome than a lawful battle. Happy Kshatriya, O son of Prithâ, find such a battle as this, come of itself, an open door to heaven.

devverse:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं खर्गद्वारमपावृतम् ।
सुखिन: क्षत्रिया: पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ।। ३२ ॥
अथ चेत्त्वमिर्मं घर्म्यं सङ्गामं न करिष्यसि ।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३३ ॥
commentary: Now if thou wouldst not fight this lawful battle, then, having abandoned thine own duty and fame, thou shalt incur sin. If, on the other hand, you will not fight this battle which is enjoined on you as a duty, and which is not opposed to Law, you will, by neglecting this battle, have abandoned your duty and lost the fame that you acquired by your encounter with such persons as Mahadeva. * Thus you will only incur sin.

devverse:
अर्कार्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्।
सम्भावितस्य चाक्रीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥ ३४ ॥
commentary: People, too, will recount thy everlasting infamy; and, to one who has been esteemed, infamy is more than death.

devverse:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥ ३५ ॥
commentary: The great car-warriors will think thou hast withdrawn from the battle through fear; and, having been (hitherto) highly esteemed by them, thou wilt incur their contempt.

devverse:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः ।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम ॥ ३६ ॥
commentary: Thy enemies, too, scorning thy power, will take many abusive words. What is more pain- ful than that ?

devverse:
हतो वा प्राप्ससि खर्ग जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम ।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥ ३० ॥
commentary: Killed, thou wilt reach heaven; victorious, thou wilt enjoy the earth. Wherefore, O son of Kunti, arise, resolved to fight.

devverse:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥ ३८ ॥
commentary: Then, treating alike pleasure and pain, gain and loss, success and defeat, prepare for the battle, and thus wilt thou not incur sin.

devverse:
एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्खये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां ऋणु ।
बुध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥ ३९ ॥
commentary: This, which has been taught to thee is wisdom concerning Sankhya. Now listen to wisdom concerning Yoga, which possessing thou shalt cast off the bond of action.

devverse:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रखवायो न विद्यते ।
खल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात ॥ ४० ॥
commentary: There is no loss of effort here, there is no harm. Even a little of this devotion delivers one from great fear.

devverse:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन ।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥ ४१ ॥
commentary: Here, O son of Kuru, there is one thought of a resolute nature. Many-branched and endless are the thoughts of the irresolute.

devverse:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः ।
वेदवादरता: पार्थं नान्यदस्तीति वादिन: ।। ४२ ।।
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् ।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ।। ४३ ।।
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयाऽपहृतचेतसाम् ।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाघौ न विधीयते ॥ ४४ ॥
commentary: 42-44. No conviction of a resolute nature is formed in the mind of those who are attached to pleasures and power, and whose minds are drawn away by that flowery speech which the unwise- enamoured of Vedic utterances, declaring there is nothing else, full of desire, having svarga as their goal-utter, (a speech) which promises birth as the reward of actions and which abounds in speci- fic acts for the attainment of pleasure and power, O son of Pritha.

devverse:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्नैगुण्यो भवार्जुन ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥ ४५ ॥
commentary: The Vedas treat of the triad of the gunas. Be, O Arjuna, free from the triad of the gunas, free from pairs, free from acquisition and preservation, ever remaining in the Sattva (Good- ness), and self-possessed.

devverse:
याबानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्छतोदके ।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥ ४६ ॥
commentary: What utility there is in a reservoir by the side of an all-spreading flood of water, the same (utility) there is in all Vedas for an enlightened Brahmana.

devverse:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफल्रहेतुर्भूमा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ ४७ ॥
commentary: Thy concern is with action alone, never with results. Let not the fruit of action be thy motive, nor let thy attachment be for inaction.

devverse:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्तवा घनञ्जय ।
सिद्धचासिच्द्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥ ४८ ॥
commentary: Steadfast in devotion do thy works, O Dhanamjaya, casting off attachment, being the same in success and failure. Evenness is called Yoga.

devverse:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्त्रिच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥ ४९ ॥
commentary: Verily action is far inferior to devotion in wisdom (buddhi-yoga), O Dhanamjaya. In wisdom (buddhi) seek thou shelter. Wretched are they whose motive is the fruit.

devverse:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उमे सुक्कतदुष्कृते ।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥ ५० ॥
commentary: He who is endued with wisdom casts off here both good deeds and bad deeds. Wherefore apply thyself to devotion. In regard to actions devotion is a power.

devverse:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥ ५१ ॥
commentary: For, men of wisdom cast off the fruit of action; possessed of knowledge (and) released from the bond of birth, they go to the place where there is no evil.

devverse:
यदा ते मोहकछिछं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति ।
तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥ ५२ ॥
commentary: When thy mind shall cross beyond the mire of delusion, then wilt thou attain to a disgust of what is yet to be heard and what has been heard.

devverse:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला ।
समाधावचळा बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यासि ॥ ५३ ॥
commentary: When thy mind, perplexed by what thou hast heard, shall stand firm and steady in the Self, then wilt thou attain Yoga.

devverse:
श्चितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्वस्य केशव ।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत ब्रजेत किम् ॥ ५४ ॥
commentary: What, O Kesava!, is the description of one of steady knowledge, who is constant in con- templation? How does one of steady knowledge speak, how sit, how move?

devverse:
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान् ।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥ ५५ ॥
commentary: When a man, satisfied in the Self alone by himself, completely casts off all the desires of the mind, then is he said to be one of steady knowledge.

devverse:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः ।
वीतरागभयक्रोघः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥ ५६ ॥
commentary: He whose heart is not distressed in cala- mities, from whom all longing for pleasures has departed, who is free from attachment, fear and wrath, he is called a sage, a man of steady know- ledge.

devverse:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य ग्लभाञ्चभम् ।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५७ ॥
commentary: Whoso, without attachment anywhere, on meeting with anything good or bad, neither exults nor hates, his knowledge becomes steady.

devverse:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ५८ ॥
commentary: When he completely withdraws the senses from sense-objects, as the tortoise (withdraws) its limbs from all sides, his knowledge is steady.

devverse:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः ।
रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥ ५९ ॥
commentary: Objects withdraw from an abstinent man, but not the taste. On seeing the Supreme, his taste, too, ceases.

devverse:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ।
इन्द्रियानि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसमं मनः ॥ ६० ॥
commentary: The dangerous senses, O son of Kunti, forcibly carry away the mind of a wise man, even while striving (to control them).

devverse:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्पर: ।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ ६१ ॥
commentary: Restraining them all, a man should remain steadfast, intent on Me. His knowledge is steady whose senses are under control.

devverse:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।
सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोघोऽभिजायते ॥ ६२ ॥
commentary: When a man thinks of objects, attachment for them arises. From attachment arises desire; from desire arises wrath.

devverse:
ऋोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः ।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणत्रयति ॥ ६३ ॥
commentary: From wrath arises delusion; from delu- sion, failure of memory; from failure of memory, loss of conscience; from loss of conscience he is utterly ruined.

devverse:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् ।
आत्मवरयैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥ ३४ ॥
commentary: He attains peace, who, self-controlled, approaches objects with the senses devoid of love and hatred and brought under his own-control.

devverse:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते ।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याञ्च बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥ ६५ ॥
commentary: In peace there is an end of all his miseries; for, the reason of the tranquil-minded soon be- comes steady.

devverse:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥ ६६ ॥
commentary: There is no wisdom to the unsteady, and no meditation to the unsteady, and to the unmedi- tative no peace; to the peaceless, how can there be happiness?

devverse:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनु विधीयते ।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावामिवाम्भासि ॥ ६७ ॥
commentary: For, the mind which yields to the roving senses carries away his knowledge, as the wind (carries away) a ship on water. Therefore, O mighty-armed, his knowledge is steady whose senses have been entirely restrain- ed from sense-objects.

devverse:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेम्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ।। ६८ ॥
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।
यस्यां जान्नति भूतानि सा निशा परयतो मुनेः ॥ ६९ ॥
commentary: What is night to all beings, therein the self controlled one is awake. Where all beings are awake, that is the night of the sage who sees.

devverse:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं
समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविज्ञान्ति सर्वे
स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥ ७० ॥
commentary: He attains peace, into whom all desires enter as waters enter the ocean, which, filled from all sides, remains unaltered ; but not he who desires objects.

devverse:
विहाय कामान्य: सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः ।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥ ७१ ॥
commentary: That man attains peace, who, abandoning all desires, moves about without attachment, with- out selfishness, without vanity.

devverse:
एषा बाह्मी स्थिति: पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।
स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकाळेऽपि ब्रह्म निर्वाणमृच्छति ॥ ७२ ॥
commentary: This is the Brahmic state, O son of Pri- tha. Attaining to this, none is deluded. Remaining in this state even at the last period of life, one at- tains to the felicity of Brahman. KARMA-YOGA.

devverse:
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन ।
तर्तिक कर्माणे घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥ १ ॥
commentary: If it be thought by Thee that knowledge is superior to action, O Janardana, why then dost Thou, O Kesava, direct me to this terrible action?

devverse:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे ।
तदेकं वद निश्चिल येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्तुयाम् ॥ २ ॥
commentary: With an apparently perplexing speech, Thou confusest as it were my understanding. Tell me with certainty that one (way) by which.I may attain bliss.

devverse:
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविघा निष्ठा पुरा पोक्ता मयाऽनव ।
ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्खयानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥ ३ ॥
commentary: In this world a twofold path was taught by Me at first, O sinless one: that of Sankhyas by devotion to knowledge, and that of Yogins by devotion to action.

devverse:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽइनुते ।
न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥ ४ ॥
commentary: Not by abstaining from action does man win actionlessness, nor by mere renunciation does he attain perfection.

devverse:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जात तिष्ठयकर्मकत ।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥ ५ ॥
commentary: None, verily, even for an instant, ever remains doing no action; for every one is driven helpless to action by the energies born of Nature.

devverse:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् ।
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥ ६ ॥
commentary: He who, restraining the organs of action, sits thinking in his mind of the objects of the senses, self-deluded, he is said to be one of false conduct.

devverse:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन ।
कर्मेन्दियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥ ७ ॥
commentary: But whoso, restraining the senses by mind O Arjuna, engages in Karma-Yoga, unattached, with organs of action, he is esteemed.

devverse:
नियतं करु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः ।
शरीरयात्राऽपि च ते न प्रसिघ्येदकर्मण: ॥ ८ ॥
commentary: Do thou perform (thy) bounden duty; for action is superior to inaction. And even the main- tenance of the body would not be possible for thee by inaction.

devverse:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः ।
तद्र्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥ ९ ॥
commentary: Except in the case of action for Sacrifice's sake, this world is action-bound. Action for the sake Thereof, do thou, O son of Kunti, perform, free from attachment.

devverse:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्टा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः ।
अनेन प्रसाविष्यव्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामघुक्रु ॥ १० ॥
commentary: Having first created mankind together with sacrifices, the Prajapati said, "By this shall ye propagate; let this be to you the cow of plenty.

devverse:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः ।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥ ११ ॥
commentary: With this do ye nourish the Gods, and the Gods shall nourish you; thus nourishing one another, ye shall attain the supreme good.

devverse:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवो दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः ।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो सुइके स्तेन एव सः ॥ १२ ॥
commentary: "Nourished by the sacrifice, the Gods shall indeed bestow on you the enjoyments ye desire." Whoso enjoys-without offering to Them -Their gifts, he is verily a thief.

devverse:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वाकलिबर्षेः ।
अञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥ १३ ॥
commentary: The righteous, who eat the remnant of the sacrifice, are freed from all sins; but sin do the impious eat who cook for their own sakes.

devverse:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः ।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥ १४ ॥

कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ १५ ॥
commentary: 14-15. From food creatures come forth; the production of food is from rain; rain comes forth from sacrifice; sacrifice is born of action; know thou that action comes from Brahman, and that Brahman comes from the Imperishable. There- fore, the all-pervading Brahman ever rests in sacrifice.

devverse:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः ।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थं स जीवति ॥ १६ ॥
commentary: He who follows not here the wheel thus set in motion, who is of sinful life, indulging in senses, he lives in vain, O son of Pritha.

devverse:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मनृप्तश्च मानवः ।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥ १७ ॥
commentary: That man, verily, who rejoices only in the Self, who is satisfied with the Self, who is con- tent in the Self alone,-for him there is nothing to do.

devverse:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन ।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिद्र्थेव्यपाश्रयः ॥ १८ ॥
commentary: For him, there is here no interest what- ever in what is done or what is not done. Nor is there in all beings any one ne should resort to for any object.

devverse:
तस्मादसक्त: सततं कार्यं कर्म समावर ।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पुरुषः ॥ १९ ॥
commentary: Therefore, without attachment, constant- ly perform the action which should be done; for, performing action without attachment, man reaches the Supreme.

devverse:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः ।
लोकसंङ्ग्रहमेवापि सम्परयन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ २० ॥
commentary: By action only, indeed, did Janaka and others try to attain perfection. Even with a view to the protection of the masses thou shouldst per- form (action).

devverse:
यद्याचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तद्नुवर्तते ॥ २१ ॥
commentary: Whatsoever a great man does, that alone the other men do; whatever he sets up as the standard, that the world follows.

devverse:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन ।
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्ते एव च कर्मणि ॥ २२ ॥
commentary: I have nothing whatsoever to achieve in the three worlds, O son of Pritha, nor is there any- thing unattained that should be attained; yet I engage in action.

devverse:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः ।
मम वत्मीनुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थं सर्वेशः ॥ २३ ॥
commentary: For, should I not ever engage in action, unwearied, men would in all matters follow My path, O son of Pritha.

devverse:
उत्सीदेयरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् ।
सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥ २४ ॥
commentary: These worlds would be ruined if I should not perform action; I should be the cause of confusion of castes, and should destroy these creatures.

devverse:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत ।
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथाऽसक्तश्चिकीर्कुलेकसङ्ग्हम् ॥ २५ ॥
commentary: As ignorant men act attached to work, O Bhârata, so should the wise man act, unattached from a wish to protect the masses.

devverse:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् ।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ॥ २६ ॥
commentary: Let no wise man cause unsettlement in the minds of the ignorant who are attached to action; he should make them do all actions, him- self fulfilling them with devotion.

devverse:
प्रकृते: क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वेशः ।
अहङ्काराविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥ २७ ॥
commentary: Actions are wrought in all cases by the energies of Nature. He whose mind is deluded by egoism thinks 'I am the doer.'

devverse:
तत्त्ववितु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः ।
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥ २८ ॥
commentary: But he who knows the truth, O mighty- armed, about the divisions of the energies and (their) functions, is not attached, thinking that the energies act upon the energies.

devverse:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु ।
तानकरस्रविदो मन्दान्करस्रविन्न विचालयेत् ॥ २९ ॥
commentary: Those deluded by the energies of Nature are attached to the functions of the energies. He who knows the All should not unsettle the unwise who know not the All.

devverse:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा ।
निराशीनिर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतब्बरः ॥ ३० ॥
commentary: Renouncing all action in Me, with thy thought resting on the Self, being free from hope, free from selfishness, devoid of fever, do thou fight.

devverse:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः ।
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥ ३१ ॥
commentary: Men who constantly practise this teach- ing of Mine with faith and without cavilling, they too are liberated from actions.

devverse:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् ।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥ ३२ ॥
commentary: But those who, carping at this, My teaching, practise it not,-know them as deluded in all knowledge, as senseless men doomed to destruction.

devverse:
सदृशं चेष्टते खस्याः प्रकृतेज्ञीनवानपि ।
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निन्नहः किं करिष्यति ॥ ३३ ॥
commentary: Even the man of knowledge acts in con- formity with his own nature; (all) beings follow (their) nature; what shall coercion avail?

devverse:
इन्द्रियस्योन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ ।
तयोर्न वज्ञमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥ ३४ ॥
commentary: Love and hate lie towards the object of each sense; let none become subject to these two; for, they are his enemies.

devverse:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
खधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥ ३५ ॥
commentary: Better one's own duty, though devoid of merit, than the duty of another well discharged. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is productive of danger.

devverse:
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः ।
अनिच्छन्नापि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥ ३६ ॥
commentary: But by what dragged on, O Varshneya, does a man, though reluctant, commit sin, as if constrained by force ?

devverse:
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ।
महाज्ञनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥ ३७ ॥
commentary: It is desire, it is wrath, born of the energy of Rajas, all-devouring, all sinful; that, know thou, is the foe here.

devverse:
धूमेनात्रियते वह्रिर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च ।
ं ययोस्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तया तेनेदमावृतम् ॥ ३८ ॥
commentary: As fire is surrounded by smoke, as a mirror by rust, as the foetus is enclosed in the womb, so is this covered by it.

devverse:
आवतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा ।
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥ ३९ ॥
commentary: Covered, O son of Kunti, is wisdom by this constant enemy of the wise, in the form of desire, which is greedy and insatiable.

devverse:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते ।
एतैर्विमोहयत्वेष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥ ४० ॥
commentary: The senses, mind, and reason are said to be its seat; veiling wisdom through these, it deludes the embodied.

devverse:
तस्मास्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ ।
पाप्सानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाञ्चनम् ॥ ४१ ॥
commentary: Therefore, O lord of the Bharatas, restrain the senses first, do thou cast off this sinful thing which is destructive of knowledge and wisdom.

devverse:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेम्यः परं मनः ।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तुं सः ॥ ४२ ॥
commentary: They say that the senses are superior ; superior to the senses is mind; superior to mind is reason; one who is even superior to reason is He.

devverse:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्धा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना ।
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥ ४३ ॥
commentary: Then knowing Him who is superior to reason, subduing the self by the self, slay thou, O mighty-armed, the enemy in the form of desire. hard to conquer. JNANA-YOGA.

devverse:
इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् ।
विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिङ्वाकवेऽन्रवीत् ॥ १ ॥
commentary: I taught this imperishable Yoga to Vivas- vat; Vivasvat taught it to Manu; Manu taught to Ikshvâku.

devverse:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः ।
स काल्रेनेह महता योगो नष्ट: परन्तप ॥ २ ॥
commentary: This, handed down thus in succession, the King-sages learnt, This Yoga, by long lapse of time, has been lost here, O harasser of foes.

devverse:
स एवाऽयं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः ।
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥ ३ ॥
commentary: That same ancient Yoga has been to-day taught to thee by Me, seeing that thou art My devotee and friend; for, this is the Supreme Secret.

devverse:
अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वत: ।
कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥ ४ ॥
commentary: Later is Thy birth, and prior the birth of Vivasvat; how am I to understand that Thou taughtest this Yoga in the beginning ?

devverse:
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन ।
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥ ५ ॥
commentary: Many births of Mine have passed, as well as of thine, O Arjuna; all these I know, thou know- es not, O harasser of foes.

devverse:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् ।
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया ॥ ६ ॥
commentary: Though I am unborn, of imperishable nature, and though I am the Lord of all beings, yet ruling over My own nature, I am born by My own Mâyâ.

devverse:
यदा यदा हि घर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत ।
अम्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥ ७ ॥
commentary: Whenever there is a decay of religion, O Bharata, and an ascendency of irreligion, then I manifest Myself.

devverse:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥ ८ ॥
commentary: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, for the firm establishment of religion, I am born in every age.

devverse:
जन्म कम च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
त्यक्तवा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥ ९ ॥
commentary: Whoso knows thus My divine birth and action in truth is not born again on leaving this body; he comes to Me, O Arjuna.

devverse:
वीतरागभयकोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः ।
बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥ १० ॥
commentary: Free from passion, fear and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, purified by the fire (tapas) of wisdom, many have reached My being.

devverse:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।
मम वत्मोनुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थं सर्वेशः ॥ ११ ॥
commentary: Howsoever men approach Me, even so do I reward them; My path do men follow in all things O son of Pritha.

devverse:
काङ्कन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः ।
क्षिपं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्मवति कर्मजा ॥ १२ ॥
commentary: They who long after success in actions sacrifice here to the Gods : for, soon in this world of man accrues success from action.

devverse:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः ।
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विख्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥ १३ ॥
commentary: The fourfold caste has been created by according to the distribution of energies and ons; though I am the author thereof, know Me on-agent and immutable.

devverse:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पूहा ।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मेभिने स बख्यते ॥ १४ ॥
commentary: Actions pollute Me not, nor have I a desire for the fruit of actions. He who knows Me thus is not bound by actions.

devverse:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वेरपि मुमुक्षभिः ।
कुरु कमैंव तस्मारवं पूर्वे: पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥ १५ ॥
commentary: Thus knowing, men of old performed ac- tion in the hope of liberation: therefore do thou also perform action as did the ancients in the olden time.

devverse:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः ।
तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽग्लभात् ॥ १६ ॥
commentary: What is action? What is inaction-As to this, even the wise are deluded I shall teach thee such action, by knowing which thou shalt be liberated from evil.

devverse:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः ।
अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥ १७ ॥
commentary: For, thou hast to know something even of action, something to know of unlawful action, and something to know of inaction; hard to under- stand is the nature of action.

devverse:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पत्रयेदकर्माणि च कर्म यः ।
स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः क्रत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥ १८ ॥
commentary: He who can see inaction in action, who can also see action in inaction, he is wise among men, he is devout, he is the performer of all action.

devverse:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः ।
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाड्डः पण्डितं बुघाः ॥ १९ ॥
commentary: He whose engagements are all devoid of desires and purposes, and whose actions have been burnt by the fire of wisdom, him the wise call a sage.

devverse:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यनृप्तो निराश्रयः ।
कर्मण्याभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥ २० ॥
commentary: Having abandoned attachment for the fruits of action, ever content, dependent on none, though engaged in actions, nothing at all does he do.

devverse:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिप्रहः ।
ज्ञारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ २१ ॥
commentary: Free from desire, with the mind and the self controlled, having relinquished all possessions doing mere bodily action, he incurs no sin.

devverse:
यहच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः ।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वाऽपि न निबद्ध्यते ॥ २२ ॥
commentary: Satisfied with what comes to him by chance, rising above the pairs of opposites, free from envy, equanimous in success and failure, though acting he is not bound.

devverse:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः ।
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समयं प्रविछीयते ॥ २३ ॥
commentary: Of the man whose attachment is gone, who is liberated, whose mind is established in know- ledge, who acts for the sake of sacrifice,—his whole action melts away.

devverse:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविब्रह्मामौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् ।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥ २४ ॥
commentary: Brahman is the offering, Brahman the oblation; by Brahman is the oblation poured into the fire of Brahman; Brahman verily shall be reached by him who always sees Brahman in action.

devverse:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते ।
ब्रह्माप्रावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥ २५ ॥
commentary: Other yogins resort to sacrifices to Gods: in the fire of Brahman others offer the Self by the Self.

devverse:
श्रोत्राद्गिनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति ।
शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥ २६ ॥
commentary: Others offer hearing and other senses in the fires of restraint; others offer sound and other objects in the fires of the senses.

devverse:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे ।
आत्मसंयमयोगामौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥ २७ ॥
commentary: And others sacrifice all the functions of the senses and the functions of the vitality in the wisdom-kindled fire of the Yoga of Self-restraint.

devverse:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपायज्ञा यागयज्ञास्तथाऽपरे ।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितत्रताः ॥ २८ ॥
commentary: THE BHAGAVAD GITA. Others are sacrificers by their wealth, sacrificers by austerity, sacrificers by Yogas, sacri- ficers by reading and knowledge, ascetics of rigid vows.

devverse:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे ।
प्राणापानगती रुव्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥ २९ ॥
commentary: Others offer pråna (outgoing breath) in apâna (incoming breath), and apâna in prâna, restraining the passages of prâna and apâna, absorbed in prânâyâma (restraint of breath).

devverse:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति ।
सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञाविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥ ३० ॥
commentary: Others, with regulated food, offer life- breaths in life-breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins are destroyed by sacrifice.

devverse:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
नायं छोकोऽस्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥ ३१ ॥
commentary: Eating of ambrosia, the remnant of the sacrifice, they go to Eternal Brahman. This world is not for the non-sacrificer; whence the other?-O best of Kurus.

devverse:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे ।
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोस्यसे ॥ ३२ ॥
commentary: Thus manifold sacrifices are spread at the mouth of Brahman. Know them all as born of action. Thus knowing, thou shalt be liberated.

devverse:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञ: परन्तप ।
सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥ ३३ ॥
commentary: Superior is wisdom-sacrifice to the sacri- fice with objects, O harasser of thy foes. All action, without exception, O son of Prithâ, is comprehended in wisdom.

devverse:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया ।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥ ३४ ॥
commentary: Know this: by long prostration, by enquiry, by service, those men of wisdom who have realised the truth will teach thee wisdom.

devverse:
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव ।
येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रव्त्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥ ३५ ॥
commentary: Knowing which, thou shalt not again thus fall into error, O Pandava; and by which, thou wilt see all beings in thy Self and also in Me.

devverse:
अपि चेदसि पापेम्यः सर्वेम्यः पापकृत्तमः ।
सर्वे।ज्ञानप्तवेनैन वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥ ३६ ॥
commentary: Even shouldst thou be the most sinful of all the sinful, thou shalt verily cross all sin by the bark of wisdom. How does wisdom destroy sin ?—Here is an example:

devverse:
यथैघांसि समिद्घोऽग्निभस्ससात्कुरुतेऽजुन ।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥ ३७ ॥
commentary: As kindled fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so does wisdom-fire reduce all actions to ashes.

devverse:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
तत्खयं योगसंसिद्धः काल्रेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥ ३८ ॥
commentary: Verily, there exists here no purifier equal to wisdom. He who is perfected by Yoga finds it in time in himself by himself.

devverse:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
ज्ञानं लब्ब्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ३९ ॥
commentary: He obtains wisdom who is full of faith. who is devoted to it, and who has subdued the senses. Having obtained wisdom, he ere long attains to the Supreme Peace.

devverse:
अज्ञआश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति ।
नायं लेकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संज्ञयात्मनः ॥ ४० ॥
commentary: The ignorant, the faithless, and one of doubting self, is ruined. There is neither this world, nor the other, nor happiness, for one of doubting self.

devverse:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्ज्ञिसंशयम् ।
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबघ्नन्ति धनंजय ॥ ४१ ॥
commentary: Him who has renounced actions by Yoga, whose doubts have been cloven asunder by wisdom, who is self-possessed, actions bind not, O Dhanamjaya.

devverse:
तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः ।
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥ ४२ ॥
commentary: Therefore with the sword of wisdom cleave asunder this doubt of the Self lying in the heart and born of ignorance, and resort to Yoga. Arise, O Bharata. SAMNYASA-YOGA

devverse:
संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंललि ।
यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रुहि सुनिश्चितम् ॥ १ ॥
commentary: Renunciation of actions, O Krishna, Thou praisest, and again Yoga. Tell me conclusively that which is the better of the two.

devverse:
संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुमौ ।
तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥ २ ॥
commentary: Renunciation and Yoga through action both lead to the highest bliss; but, of the two, Yoga through action is esteemed more than renunciation of action.

devverse:
ज्ञेय: स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न कारूक्षाति ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
commentary: He should be known as a perpetual renouncer who neither hates nor desires ; for, free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily set free from bondage.

devverse:
साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः ।
एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलगु ॥ ४ ॥
commentary: Children, not the wise, speak of Sankhya and Yoga as distinct. He who is rightly devoted to even one obtains the fruits of both.

devverse:
यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते ।
एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पत्र्यति स पत्र्यति ॥ ५ ॥
commentary: That state which is reached by Sankhyas is reached by Yogins also. He sees, who sees Sankhya and Yoga as one.

devverse:
संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः ।
योगयुक्तो मुनिब्रेह्म न चिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ६ ॥
commentary: But renunciation, O mighty-armed, is hard to attain except by Yoga; a sage equipped with Yoga ere long reaches Brahman.

devverse:
योगयुक्तो विद्युद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः ।
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नवि न लिप्यते ॥ ७ ॥
commentary: He who is equipped with Yoga, whose mind is quite pure, by whom the self has been conquer- ed, whose senses have been subdued, whose Self has become the Self of all beings,-though doing, he is not tainted.

devverse:
नैव किञ्चित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् ।
पश्यन्श्युण्वन्स्पृशञ्जिघन्नश्रनगच्छन्श्वसन्स्वपन् ॥ ८ ॥

प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृहन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि ।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन् ॥ ९ ॥
commentary: 8-9. 'I do nothing at all'; thus would the truth-knower think, steadfast,-though seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, breathing, speaking, letting go, seizing, opening and closing the eyes,-remembering that the senses move among sense-objects.

devverse:
ब्रह्मण्याघाय कर्माणि सङ्गं लक्त्वा करोति यः ।
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भला ॥ १० ॥
commentary: He who does actions, offering them to Brahman, abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, as a lotus leaf by water.

devverse:
कायेन मनसा बुद्धचा केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि ।
योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मग्लुद्धये ॥ ११ ॥
commentary: By the body, by the mind, by the intellect, by mere senses also, Yogins perform action, without attachment, for the purification of the self.

devverse:
युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् ।
अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥ १२ ॥
commentary: The steady-minded one, abandoning the fruit of action, attains the peace born of devotion. The unsteady one, attached to the fruit through the action of desire, is firmly bound.

devverse:
सर्वकर्माणि मनसा सन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी ।
नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् ॥ १३ ॥
commentary: Renouncing all actions by thought, and Self-controlled, the embodied one rests happily in the nine-gated city, neither at all acting nor causing to act.

devverse:
न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि छोकस्य सृजति प्रमुः ।
न कर्मफळसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते ॥ १४ ॥
commentary: Neither agency nor objects does the Lord create for the world, nor union with the fruits of actions. But it is the nature that acts.

devverse:
नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः ।
अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुद्यान्ति जन्तवः ॥ १५ ॥
commentary: The Lord takes neither the evil nor even the good deed of any; wisdom is enveloped by un- wisdom; thereby mortals are deluded.

devverse:
ज्ञानेन तु तद्ज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः ।
तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥ १६ ॥
commentary: But to those whose unwisdom is destroy- ed by wisdom of the Self, like the sun wisdom illuminates that Supreme.

devverse:
तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः ।
गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः ॥ १७ ॥
commentary: With their consciousness in That, their Self being That, intent on That, with That for their supreme goal, they go never again to return, their sins shaken off by means of wisdom.

devverse:
विद्याविनयसम्पन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि ।
ञ्चानि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥ १८ ॥
commentary: In a Brahmana endued with wisdom and humility, in a cow, in an elephant, as also in a dog and in a dog-eater,* the wise see the same.

devverse:
इहैव तैर्जित: सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः ।
निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्वह्मणि ते स्थिता: ॥ १९ ॥
commentary: Even here birth is overcome by them whose mind rests on equality. Spotless, indeed, and equal is Brahman; wherefore in Brahman they rest.

devverse:
न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् ।
स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्माविद्बह्माणि स्थितः ॥ २० ॥
commentary: He who knows Brahman can neither rejoice on obtaining the pleasant, nor grieve on obtaining the unpleasant,-steady-minded, un- deluded, resting in Brahman.

devverse:
बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् ।
स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षय्यमइतुते ॥ २१ ॥
commentary: With the self unattached to external contacts, he finds the joy which is in the Self; with the Self engaged in the contemplation of Brahman he attains the endless joy. For, those delights which are born of contacts are only generators of pain, having a be- ginning and an end, O son of Kunti; a wise man rejoices not in them.

devverse:
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते ।
आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ।। २२ ।।
शकोर्ताहैव यः सोढुं पाक् शरीरविमोक्षणात् ।
कामक्रोघोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुली नरः ॥ २३ ॥
commentary: He that is able, while still here, to with- stand, before liberation from the body, the impulse of desire and anger, he is a Yogin, he is a happy man.

devverse:
योऽन्तः सुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः ।
स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥ २४ ॥
commentary:
Whoso has his joy within and his pastime within, and whoso has his light within only,
that Yogin attains Brahman's bliss, himself be- coming Brahman.

devverse:
लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः ।
छिन्नद्वैघा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥ २५ ॥
commentary: The sages attain Brahman's bliss,-they whose sins have been destroyed and doubts remov- ed, who are self-controlled and intent on the welfare of all beings.

devverse:
कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाय ।
अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥ २६ ॥
commentary: To the devotees who are free from desire and anger, who have controlled their thought, and who have known the Self, Brahman's bliss exists everywhere.

devverse:
स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यां अञ्जुन्नैवान्तरे अवोः ।
प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ ॥ २७ ॥

यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः ।
विगतेच्छाभयकोघो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥ २८ ॥
commentary: 27-28. Shutting out all external contracts and fixing the sight between the eye-brows, equalising the out-going and the in-going breaths which pass through the nostrils, controlling the senses, mind and intellect, having moksha as his highest goal, free from desire, fear and anger,-the sage who ever (remains thus) is verily liberated.

devverse:
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वेलोकमहेश्वरम् ।
सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥ २९ ॥
commentary: On knowing Me,-the Lord of all sacrifices and austerities, the Great Lord of all Worlds, the Friend of all beings,-he goes to Peace. DHYANA-YOGA.

devverse:
अनाश्रित: कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति य:।
स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरमिर्न चाकिय: ॥ १ ॥
commentary: He who, without depending on the fruits of action, performs his bounden duty, he is a Samnyasin and a Yogin : not he who is without fire and without action.

devverse:
यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव ।
न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्करणो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥ २ ॥
commentary: Do thou, O Pandava, know Yoga to be that which they call renunciation; no one, verily, becomes a Yogin who has not reno unced thoughts.

devverse:
आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्मं कारणमुच्यते ।
योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
commentary: For a devotee who wishes to attain to Yoga, action is said to be the means. For the same (devotee), when he has attained to Yoga, quiescence (sama) is said to be the means.

devverse:
यदा हि चेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते ।
सर्वसङ्करपसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥ ४ ॥
commentary: When a man, renouncing all thoughts, is not attached to sense-objects and actions, then he is said to have attained to Yoga.

devverse:
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥ ५ ॥
commentary: Let a man raise himself by himself, let him not lower himself; for, he alone is the friend of himself, he alone is the enemy of himself. To him who has conquered himself by himself, his own self is the friend of himself, but to him who has not (conquered) himself, his own self stands in the place of an enemy like the (external) foe.

devverse:
बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य थेनात्मैवात्मना जितः ।
अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ।। ६ ॥
जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः ।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानावमानयोः ॥ ७ ॥
commentary: The self-controlled and serene man's Supreme Self is steadfast in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, as also in honour and disgrace.

devverse:
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः ।
युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाइमकाक्चनः ॥ ८ ॥
commentary: The Yogin whose self is satisfied with knowledge and wisdom, who remains unshaken, who has conquered the senses, he is said to be a saint,-for whom a lump of earth, a stone and gold are equal.

devverse:
सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्रद्वेष्यबन्धुषु ।
साघुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥ ९ ॥
commentary: He is esteemed, who is of the same mind to the good-hearted, friends, foes, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, relatives, the righteous, and the unrighteous.

devverse:
योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः ।
एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपारिग्रहः ॥ १० ॥
commentary: Let the Yogin try constantly to keep the mind steady, remaining in seclusion, alone, with the mind and body controlled, free from desire, and having no possessions.

devverse:
ञ्जवौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः ।
नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चेळाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥ ११ ॥
commentary: Having in a cleanly spot established a firm seat, neither too high nor too low, with cloth. skin, and kusa grass thereon;

devverse:
तत्रैकामं मनः ऋत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियकियः ।
उपविद्यासने युड्याद्योगमात्मविद्युद्धये ॥ १२ ॥
commentary: Making the mind one-pointed, with the actions of the mind and the senses controlled, let him, seated there on the seat, practise Yoga for the purification of the self.

devverse:
समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचळं खिरः ।
सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकामं खं दिशस्त्रानवलोकयन् ॥ १३ ॥
commentary: Holding erect and still the body, the head and the neck, firm, gazing on the tip of his nose, without looking around ; Serene-minded, fearless, firm in the vow of godly life, having restrained the mind, thinking on Me, and balanced, let him sit, looking up to Me as the Supreme.

devverse:
प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीत्रीह्यचारित्रते स्थितः ।
मनः संयम्य मचित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।। १४ ॥
युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः ।
ज्ञानित निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥ १५ ॥
commentary: Thus always keeping the mind balanced, the Yogin, with the mind controlled, attains to the Peace abiding in Me, which culminates in Nirvana (moksha,)

devverse:
नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः ।
न चातिस्वप्रशीलस्य जामतो नैव चार्जुन ॥ १६ ॥
commentary: Yoga is not possible for him who eats too much, nor for him who does not eat at all, nor for him who is addicted to too much sleep, nor for him who is (ever) wakeful, O Arjuna.

devverse:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मस् ।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥ १७ ॥
commentary: To him whose food and recreation are moderate, whose exertion in actions is moderate, whose sleep and waking are moderate, to him accrues Yoga which is destructive of pain.

devverse:
यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते ।
निम्त्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥ १८ ॥
commentary: When the well-restrained thought is established in the Self only, without longing for any of the objects of desire, then he is said to be a Saint.

devverse:
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।
योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥ १९ ॥
commentary: As a lamp in a sheltered spot does not flicker,'-this has been thought as the simile of a Yogin of subdued thought, practising Yoga in the Self.

devverse:
यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया ।
यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं परयन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥ २० ॥
commentary: When thought is quiescent, restrained by the practice of Yoga; when, seeing the Self by the self, he is satisfied in his own Self;

devverse:
सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद् बुद्धिमाह्यमतीन्द्रियम् ।
वेत्ति यत्र न चैवाऽयं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥ २१ ॥
commentary: When he knows that Infinite Joy which, transcending the senses, can be grasped by reason; when, steady (in the Self), he moves never from the Reality ;

devverse:
यं लब्ब्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः ।
यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणाऽपि विचाल्यते ॥ २२ ॥
commentary: When, having obtained it, he thinks no other acquisition superior to it; when, therein established, he is not moved even by a great pain ;

devverse:
तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् ।
स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥ २३ ॥
commentary: This severance from union with pain, be it known, is called union (Yoga). That Yoga must be practised with determination and with unde- pressed heart.

devverse:
सङ्कल्पप्रमवान्कामांस्यक्त्वा सर्वानञ्चेषतः ।
मनसैवेन्द्रियमामं विनियम्य समन्ततः ॥ २४ ॥
commentary: Abandoning without reserve all fancy- born desires, well-restraining all the senses from all quarters by the mind;

devverse:
शनैःशनैरुपरमेद् बुद्धचा घृतिगृहीतया ।
आत्मसंस्यं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥ २५ ॥
commentary: Little by little let him withdraw, by reason (buddhi) held in firmness; keeping the mind established in the Self, let him not think of anything.

devverse:
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् ।
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥ २६ ॥
commentary: By whatever cause the wavering and unsteady mind wanders away, from that let him restrain it and bring it back direct under the control of the Self.

devverse:
प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् ।
उपैति ज्ञान्तरजसं ब्रह्ममूतमकल्मषम् ॥ २७ ॥
commentary: Supreme Bliss verily comes to this Yogin, whose mind is quite tranquil, whose passion is quieted, who has become Brahman, who is blemishless.

devverse:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः ।
सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमइनुते ॥ २८ ॥
commentary:
Thus always keeping the self steadfast, the Yogin, freed from sins, attains with ease to the infinite bliss of contact with the (Supreme) Brah- man. The Self abiding in all beings, and all
beings (abiding) in the Self, sees he whose self has been made steadfast by Yoga, who everywhere sees the same. He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, to him I vanish not, nor to Me does he vanish.

devverse:
सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।
ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ।। २९ ॥
यो मां पत्त्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पत्त्यति ।
तस्याहं न प्रणत्र्यामि स च मे न प्रणद्यति ।। ३० ।।
सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः ।
सर्वेथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥ ३१ ॥
commentary: Whoso, intent on unity, worships Me who abide in all beings, that Yogin dwells in Me, whatever his mode of life.

devverse:
आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पर्द्याति योऽर्जुन ।
सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः ॥ ३२ ॥
commentary: Whoso, by comparison with himself, sees the same everywhere, O Arjuna, be it pleasure or pain, he is deemed the highest Yogin.

devverse:
योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन ।
एतस्याहं न पत्र्यामि चंचलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥ ३३ ॥
commentary: This Yoga in equanimity, taught by Thee, O Destroyer of Madhu,-I see not its steady continuance, because of the restlessness (of the mind.)

devverse:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवदु दृढम् ।
तस्याऽहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥ ३४ ॥
commentary: The mind verily, is, O Krishna, restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate. Thereof the restraint I deem quite as difficult as that of the wind. Doubtless, O mighty-armed, the mind is hard to restrain and restless; but by practice, O son of Kunti, and by indifference it may be restrained.

devverse:
असंशयं महाबाहो मना दुर्निग्रहं चलम् ।
अम्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ।। ३५ ॥
असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः ।
वर्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥ ३६ ॥
commentary: Yoga, methinks is hard to attain for a man of uncontrolled self; but by him who (often) strives, self-controlled, it can be acquired by (proper) means. He who strives not, but who is possessed of faith, whose mind wanders away from Yoga,- having failed to attain perfection in Yoga, what end, O Krishna, does he meet? Having failed in both, does he not perish like a riven cloud, supportless, O mighty-armed, and perplexed in the path to Brahman?

devverse:
अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाचळितमानसः ।
अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ।। ३७ ॥
काँचन्नोभयविभ्रष्टाः व्रव्नाभ्रमिव नज्ञ्यति ।
अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ।। ३८ ॥
एतं मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमईस्यशेषतः ।
त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता नह्युपपद्यते ॥ ३९ ॥
commentary: This doubt of mine, O Krishna, do Thou dispel completely; for none other than Thyself can possibly destroy this doubt.

devverse:
पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते ।
न हि कल्याणकुत्कश्चिद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥ ४० ॥
commentary: O Partha, neither in this world nor in the next is there destruction for him; none, verily, who does good, My son, ever comes to grief. Having attained to the worlds of the righteous and having dwelt there for eternal years, he who failed in Yoga is reborn in a house of the pure and wealthy.

devverse:
प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः ।
ह्यचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ।। ४१ ।।
अथवा योगिनामेव कुळे भवति घीमताम् ।
एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥ ४२ ॥
commentary: Else, he is born in family of wise Yogins. only. This, verily, a birth like this, is very hard to obtain in this world.

devverse:
तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् ।
यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥ ४३ ॥
commentary: There he gains touch with the knowledge that was acquired in the former body and strives more than before for perfection, O son of the Kurus.

devverse:
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः ।
जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥ ४४ ॥
commentary: By that very former practice is he borne on, though unwilling. Even he who merely wishes to know of Yoga rises superior to the Word- Brahman.

devverse:
प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संद्युद्धकिल्बिषः ।
अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम ॥ ४५ ॥
commentary: Verily, a Yogin who strives with assiduity, purified from sins and perfected in the course of many births, then reaches the Supreme Goal.

devverse:
तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः ।
कर्मिभ्यइचाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥ ४६ ॥
commentary: A Yogin is deemed superior to men of austerity, and superior to even men of knowledge; he is also superior to men of action; therefore be thou a Yogin, O Arjuna.

devverse:
योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्रतेनान्तरात्मना ।
श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्तमो मतः ॥ ४७ ॥
commentary: Of all Yogins, whoso, full of faith, worships Me with his inner self abiding in Me, he is deemed by Me as most devout. VIJNANA-YOGA.

devverse:
मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थं योगं युझन्मदाश्रयः ।
असंशयं सममं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छ्रणु ॥ १ ॥
commentary: With the mind intent on Me, O Partha, practising Yoga, and finding refuge in Me, how in full without doubt thou shalt know Me, that do thou hear.

devverse:
ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवाशिष्यते ॥ २ ॥
commentary: I shall fully teach thee this knowledge combined with experience, which being known, nothing more besides here remains to be known.

devverse:
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये ।
यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वोत्ते तत्वतः ॥ ३ ॥
commentary: Among thousands of men, one perchance strives for perfection; even among those who strive and are perfect, only one perchance knows me in truth.

devverse:
अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् ।
जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं घार्यते जगत् ॥ ५ ॥
commentary: This is the inferior (Prakriti); but as distinct from this know thou My superior Prakriti, the very life, O mighty-armed, by which this universe is upheld.

devverse:
एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय ।
अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥ ६ ॥
commentary: Know that all beings have their birth in these. So, I am the source and dissolution of the whole universe.

devverse:
मत्तः परतरं नान्यतिकञ्चिदस्ति घनञ्जय ।
मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥ ७ ॥
commentary: There is naught else higher than I, O Dhananjaya: in Me all this is woven as clusters of gems on a string.

devverse:
रसोऽहमप्तु कौन्तेय प्रभाऽस्मि शशिसूर्ययोः ।
प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥ ८ ॥
commentary: I am the sapidity in water, O son of Kunti. I am the light in the moon and the sun. I am the syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in ether, humanity in men.

devverse:
पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ ।
जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपत्विषु ॥ ९ ॥
commentary: And I am the agreeable odour in the earth and the brilliance in the fire, the vitality in all beings, and I am the austerity in ascetics.

devverse:
बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थं सनातनम् ।
बुद्धिबुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥ १० ॥
commentary: Know Me, O Partha, as the eternal seed of all beings; I am the intelligence of the intelli- gent, the bravery of the brave.

devverse:
बळं बळवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् ।
धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥ ११ ॥
commentary: And of the energetic am I the energy devoid of passion and attachment; and in (all) beings I am the desire unopposed to dharma, O lord of the Bharatas.

devverse:
ये चैव सात्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाइच ये ।
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥ १२ ॥
commentary: And whatever beings are of Sattva or of Rajas or of Tamas, know them to proceed from Me: still, I am not in them, they are in me.

devverse:
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैभावरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् ।
मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥ १३ ॥
commentary: Deluded by these three (sorts of) things composed of gunas, all this world knows not Me as distinct from them and immutable.

devverse:
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया।
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥ १४ ॥
commentary: Verily this Divine Illusion of Mine, made up of gunas, is hard to surmount. Whoever seek Me alone, they cross over this Illusion.

devverse:
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराघमाः ।
मायगाऽपहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥ १५ ॥
commentary: Not Me do the evil-doers seek, the delud- ed, the vilest of men, deprived of wisdom by Illusion, following the ways of the Demons.

devverse:
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन ।
आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥ १६ ॥
commentary: Four kinds of virtuous men worship Me, O Arjuna-the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise man, O lord of the Bharatas.

devverse:
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते ।
प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रिय: ॥ १७ ॥
commentary: Of them the wise man, ever steadfast and devoted to the One, excels; for, excessively dear am I to the wise, and he is dear to Me.

devverse:
उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव में मतम् ।
आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥ १८ ॥
commentary: Noble indeed are all these; but the wise man, I deem, is the very Self; for, steadfast in mind, he resorts to Me alone as the unsurpassed goal.

devverse:
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते ।
वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्रुभः ॥ १९ ॥
commentary: At the end of many births, the man of wisdom comes to me, (realising) that Vasudeva is the all: he is the noble-souled (Mahatman), very hard to find.

devverse:
कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः ।
तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥ २० ॥
commentary: Those whose wisdom has been led away by this or that desire resort to other Gods, engag- ed in this or that rite, constrained by their own nature.

devverse:
यो यो यां यां ततुं भक्तः श्रद्धयाऽर्चितुमिच्छति ।
तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विद्घाम्यहम् ॥ २१ ॥
commentary: Whatever devotee seeks to worship with faith what form soever, that same faith of his I make unflinching.

devverse:
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्त्याराघनमीहते ।
लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हितान् ॥ २२ ॥
commentary: Possessed of that faith he engages in the worship of that (form); thence he obtains his desires, these being indeed ordained by me.

devverse:
अन्तवत्त्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेघसाम् ।
देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥ २३ ॥
commentary: That result indeed is finite, (which accrues) to those men of small intellect. Wor- shippers of Gods (Devatas) go to Gods (Devatas); My devotees come unto Me.

devverse:
अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः ।
परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥ २४ ॥
commentary: The foolish regard Me as the unmanifest- ed coming in manifestation, knowing not My higher, immutable, unsurpassed nature.

devverse:
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः ।
मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥ २५ ॥
commentary: I am not manifest to all, veiled (as I am) by Yoga-Maya. This deluded world knows not Me, unborn and imperishable. I know, O Arjuna, the past and the pre- sent and the future beings, but Me nobody knows.

devverse:
वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन ।
भावेष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ।। २६ ॥
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत ।
सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥ २७ ॥
